title: SAT2 cannot persist DAOSequence after RELEASE; restart rebinds on replayed ALLOCATE
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: robustness / correctness

m557 made process() keep last_sequence_by_eui after RELEASE so a stale RELEASE cannot drop a newer allocation. That floor is not durable.

encode_table_state() / encode_records() emit one SAT2 row per live assignment only (short, eui, expiry, sequence). After a successful RELEASE, commit() passes a sequences map that still contains the released EUI, but the encoder never writes a row without a short address. decode_table_state() therefore restores last_sequence_by_eui as empty for that EUI.

RELEASE of an EUI with no current mapping also inserts last_sequence_by_eui in memory and returns Success without commit(), so a store-backed coordinator already diverges from disk before restart.

After ALLOCATE seq=1, RELEASE seq=2, coordinator restart:
- SAT2 has no row and no sequence tombstone
- replayed ALLOCATE seq=1 is treated as a first request and rebinds the address
- in-memory, the same replay is Invalid because last_sequence is 2

lifecycle.release_survives_restart in test/vectors/short_addr_assignment.json is not covered by a restart-then-replay ALLOCATE test. Origin-signature replay (spec 8.6) can block this only if the caller used handle_origin_validated_dao and the origin floor survived; process()/handle_dao are public and do not.

Fix: persist a RELEASE tombstone (sequence without a live short), or keep sequence-only records in SAT2, and commit the unmapped-RELEASE path through the store. prune_expired() dropping sequence with the row is a related lease-expiry replay hole.
